outcomes.reason: ["The approval is conditioned on a report: 'Within 120 days after the effective date of this Code the Administrator shall make a report to the President' on the code's effect, particularly Article V, during the 90 days after its effective date, with the President's reserved power 'to make such a determination and to modify this approval in accordance therewith'. The Retail Solid Fuel Industry code's effective date is not held (no held text names this code), so neither the 90-day observation period nor the 120-day deadline can be computed, and a report date is a deadline, not an end. No held source shows whether the report was made or the President acted on it. The report direction is a one-time command to the Administrator whose first end (performance, or the June 14, 1935 repeal if it was never performed) is not established."]

["The approval runs 'for a period of 90 days, within which period the adequacy of the minimum wages established in this Code shall be given further study by the Administrator, who shall submit his report and recommendation to me for my further order'. The 90-day approval is an own-terms limit, but the order does not say when the period starts (the natural reading is the order date, February 16, 1934, giving May 16 or 17, 1934 depending on whether the day of the order is counted), and the code is also made not effective in any trade area until the five area requirements in items (1)-(5) are met, so its effective date varies by area and is not held. No held source shows whether the approval was extended, renewed or replaced by a further order after the 90 days, or whether the Administrator's report was made and acted on. The report direction and the area-by-area conditions are separate contingent commands whose first ends are not established, and a report date is a deadline, not an end."]

["Items 1 and 2 suspend Article V, Section 7 of the Restaurant Industry code 'until the first day of June, 1934, or until such time as the Administrator shall have reviewed the operation of said Code' under Article IX, Section 3 (an own-terms end no later than June 1, 1934, but the Administrator's earlier review date is not held), and item 4 suspends Article VII, Section 12 (the stop-loss provision) 'pending further investigation and report from the Code Authority and further investigation by the Administrator ... and pending further order by the Administrator'; no held order resolves item 4, so its end is not established. Item 5 provides that 'within ninety (90) days after the effective date of this Code' the Administrator may hold hearings and 'shall submit to me his report and recommendations for my further order', which would modify the approval; the code's effective date is not held, a report date is a deadline and not an end, and no held source shows whether the report was made or acted on. The order is a mixed order of suspensions pending further order and a report direction beside the approval; each such command needs its own end or a block."]

["Condition (1) requires that 'the determination of hours and wages for news department workers shall be made not later than 60 days hence' and condition (2) requires that the government members of the Code Authority 'shall report to the President not later than 60 days hence' on minors delivering and selling newspapers. Both are dated deadlines (about April 18, 1934 counting from the order's date of February 17, 1934), and a deadline is not an end. No held source shows whether the determination was made or the report delivered, so the first end of each one-time command (performance, lapse, or the June 14, 1935 repeal) is not established. EO 6613 (February 24, 1934) also modifies the approving orders for this code and the Graphic Arts code and says Article VII of this code is 'approved as submitted and without modification, condition or qualification', which bears on how condition (3), the President's comment on Article VII, stands after that date and needs its own reading."]

The shared analysis expressly leaves section 4(a) agreements and section 7(b) labor-agreement approvals undecided, and section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the provisions 'delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes', which on its face does not reach an agreement approval. No held source shows what legal effect the approved agreement had after June 14, 1935, so no end is established."]
